samples.title: Notes

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
samples.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jason Davis opens with Sammy Davis Jr. thanking the white producers for the best film ever made on black-white relations, and their cluelessness, to show that white privilege rests on an epistemology of ignorance, paralleled by the human enjoyment of ape slavery in Conquest. The chapter reads the film's plural representations - the T'Challa/Killmonger ideological tension, Nakia's 'No, I save my country' defiance of Okoye's institutional loyalty, Okoye throwing away her wig, Black viewers rooting for the 'villain' - as the kind of nuanced material that remedies decades of stereotypical representation. samples.title: We Can All Be Socratics Supreme
samples.relation: Pape uses the Ancient One's keyhole metaphor to argue that all knowledge is partial and biased: Bacon's confident scientific method ('human knowledge and human power meet in one') is itself just a useful belief, while Socratic awareness of one's ignorance — knowing that you have blind spots, even if you cannot see them — is the real wisdom. She reads the film's running gags as bias lessons (the 'Mister Doctor' exchange, Strange mistaking the wifi password 'Shamballa' for a mantra, the noble-savage prejudice) and feminist critiques of impartiality as itself partial. The whitewashing controversy around Tilda Swinton's Ancient One — weighed against the Fu Manchu stereotype of the 1963 comics and Iron Man 3's Mandarin-as-Trevor-Slattery subversion — shows how filmmakers can confront the biases they cannot simply remove.

samples.title: Psych and Philosophy

name: The Ethics of Lying and Deception

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: Taking J. L. Austin's distinction between justifying conduct (showing it was the right thing to do) and excusing it (accepting wrongdoing but denying full blame), the chapter audits the trilogy's deceptions: Blomkvist's lottery trick on the pedophile Björck, his intention to double-cross him, the fake-collapse 'double game' at Millennium, and the disinformation fed to the Section's bugs are justified, since they deceive only dangerous criminals engaged in murderous conspiracies. Salander is shakier—her hacking of the innocent Blomkvist and the tax-tip revenge on the realtor expose the flaw in 'a bastard is always a bastard' (she cannot know guilt in advance), though her lies to Bjurman, Forbes, and Zalachenko earn excuse or justification. The verdict falls hardest on the cover-up of Martin Vanger's murders—trading truth for Harriet's protection and crisis-center funding, it might have warned other women, so Blomkvist's 'unforgivable' stands—and on her final lies under oath to honest police, excusable only if she still cannot trust the state.

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: First defines lying — distinguishing it from mere error (Angela believing Peter dead), from the Haitian's non-verbal memory-wipe deception, and from Hiro's silent staging of Ando's fake death — then tests moral theories against the show's liars. Machiavelli's advice that princes may lie to keep power is played out by 'President Sylar' in 'Five Years Gone,' and the chapter finally endorses Sissela Bok's presumption against lying — a public-reasoning procedure modeled by Bob Bishop and Mohinder before Monica's virus injection.

samples.book: 077 - Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy - Bootleg This Book
samples.title: Boardwalk Empire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fallis sorts Atlantic City's lies to show which are wrong and why. Kant's and Augustine's absolute bans go too far and Grotius's life-saving exception does not apply - most of these lies get people killed - yet even altruistic lies (Margaret for Madame Jeunet and the ledger), lies told to those who want to be deceived, lies to liars, and Sorensen's bald-faced lies that no one believes (Jimmy's flat movie alibi, Rothstein's 'skilled player' whopper) remain wrong: they take informed choice out of the victim's hands, violating the Kantian autonomy that grounds the wrong of lying, and they corrode the trust on which even criminals' co-operation depends.

name: The Feminine Mystique (the problem with no name)

samples.title: 5 The Changing Bases of Sexual Politics, 1960–2020
samples.relation: Measuring women's progress since 1960 by access to the nine power bases, the chapter shows women using the size/solidarity base to launch the modern feminist movement - Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique as its manifesto, NOW as its vehicle, Ms. as its outlet and Gloria Steinem as its charismatic leader - and how law followed: the accidental Smith amendment adding sex to the 1964 Civil Rights Act, Reed and Frontiero subjecting sex classifications to scrutiny under the 14th Amendment, Griswold and Roe/Casey making reproductive control (which Justice Blackmun called 'necessary for the complete emancipation of women') a condition of women's power, and the 1970s no-fault divorce revolution that Engels's liberation program had demanded. It then charts each base statistically: the narrowing labor-force and wage gaps, women's still minor share of the bourgeoisie, the reversal of the college gender gap and Women's Studies programs built on the Black Studies model, women's entry into cabinet, Court, Congress, clergy and the military, secularization that weakens the religion base behind Elizabeth Cady Stanton's old challenge, and a new moral consensus that unequal treatment of women is wrong.

samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Sirvent and Baker read The Book of Mormon alongside 'Cartman Sucks' and 'The Biggest Douche in the Universe' to expose religious fundamentalism—Elder Price's 'I Believe' creed, Elder McKinley's 'turn it off' cure for gay feelings, the conversion camp that is 'fixing' Bradley—as at once naive and arrogant. samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy

He reads Spider's 'schizo-phonetic partition' and Tom/Joey's shifting use of 'I' in A History of Violence as Lacanian 'empty speech' and the narcissistic 'monument' of a censored unconscious chapter that resurfaces; Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Moore's paradox recast Joey's split as an illegitimate private language game, and Deleuze/Guattari's account of the other as a 'possible world' reframes the frightened face on the cinema screen.

samples.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
samples.title: Monstrous motherhood
samples.relation: The chapter argues that horror films about mothers are not static representations but Foucauldian sites where 'discourses of motherhood' are produced, policed and contested; using Foucault's account of bodies disciplined through power/knowledge, it treats films as cultural artefacts that both enforce and challenge norms of 'essential' and 'ideal' motherhood. It reworks Sarah Arnold's Lacanian 'Good Mother/Bad Mother' schema (the mother who sacrifices herself so the child enters the Symbolic and submits to the Law of the Father) alongside popularised Freudian mother-blame (the 'refrigerator mother', 'tell me about your mother') to read Psycho's Norma(n), the phallic mothers of The Killing Kind and The Brood, and the doomed single mothers of The Ring, Silent Hill and Triangle. It coins the 'monstrous-maternal' to argue that motherhood is framed as always-already monstrous because no woman can meet the impossible, shifting criteria of ideal motherhood, illustrated through Grace's Vivian/Madeline generational clash and Serial Mom's Beverly Sutphin.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 12. Not Why but Who
samples.relation: Reads the mothers of Orphan Black through Freud and Lacan: Dr. Coady is the "phallic mother" at the center of the Castor clones' Oedipal drama (Rudy's kiss, the DNA trophies brought home to Mom), Tomas is Helena's abusive false father, Rachel is the child of a shattered Oedipal triangle, and the Symbolic Order that makes men active rational subjects and women passive reproductive objects is mirrored in the defects — neurological for the male clones, reproductive for the female. The chapter then brings in Luce Irigaray to show the show rewriting these stereotypes: the clones' spectrum of personalities and their constant impersonations destabilize fixed gender categories, and the many equally "real" mothers (Mrs. S., Amelia, Alison, Kendall) burst the woman-equals-womb equation. samples.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
samples.title: The Golden Power
samples.relation: Patrick Dugan reads Miyamoto's game design through Lacan: the player forms a dyad with the avatar — Link is named 'Link' precisely because he links player to system — while the wider gameworld of places and characters constitutes the social symbolic the dyad lets us explore. The Triforce symbolizes the triangular structure of this interactivity: Courage is the dyad-anchor (the player-Link bond completed by mastery), Power is the game system's trinity of sword, bomb, and arrows (whose final loop defeats Ganon in A Link to the Past), and Wisdom is the realization that all such symbolic trinities — Christian Trinity, Hindu triad, three branches of government — are representations posing as totality, with the empty center of the Triforce marking what no system captures. The 'golden power' is seeing the game being played on you, whether by designers or by society.

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reads the Cohle–Hart pairing through Lacan: Cohle is at peace with the constitutive lack introduced after the mirror stage, and his hysteric's fixation on the Other's desire is what makes him the superior interrogator, while Hart exhibits obsessional neurosis and 'interpassivity,' letting the preacher's congregation do his believing for him. Following Deleuze's Oedipal structure of detective fiction and Hegel's point that heroes are denied guilt, the chapter compares Rust to Oedipus — both men who, after a child's death, renounce the father function through anti-natalism — while arguing Cohle surpasses Oedipus by philosophically mastering the knowledge that Oedipus lacked. Rust's tying off of his 'circle of violence' is read as the Lacanian sinthome: putting his symptom to work in the service of the case rather than being destroyed by it.

samples.book: 283 - Tattoos – Philosophy for Everyone - I Ink, Therefore I Am
samples.title: TATTOOS PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE I Ink, Therefore I Am
samples.relation: Juniper Ellis shows tattoos resist any single interpretive scheme by running through cases: Loos and Lacassagne's criminological 'I tattoo, therefore I will commit murder'; the biblical Mark of Cain and St. Paul's stigmata as signs of protection and salvation; Lacan's claim that the tattoo is the first signifier that marks off the human subject; and Pacific tatau (Te Pehi Kupe's moko-as-signature, Queequeg's unreadable Moby-Dick tattoo) that incorporates a person into a collective. She reads Kant's Critique of Judgment dismissal of Maori tattooing and invokes Levinas' 'the face speaks' to argue a tattooed face is eloquent speech, crossing lines between individual and collective, saint and criminal.

samples.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
samples.title: 18. Repeating Twin Peaks
samples.relation: Komel argues repetition is both a structural principle of the TV series (every show repeats its pilot) and the key to Twin Peaks, invoking Nietzsche's eternal recurrence, Kierkegaard, and Lacan/Žižek. Using Lacan's aim-versus-goal of desire and Žižek's 'coffee without milk' as a positive absence, he reads Laura Palmer as a 'positive absence' around which the series turns, and shows the murder repetitions are out of order—Maddy's on-screen death precedes and retroactively produces Laura's in Fire Walk with Me. Laura's final scream in The Return, unlike its predecessors, subversively rewrites the original, so 'The Return' is really 'The Repetition' that undoes its origin.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 24. An Hour
samples.relation: Argues Louis's shift to an hour-a-year of digressive storytelling—spurred by George Carlin's 'dig deeper' tribute speech and forced by fatherhood—is 'secular revelation' in Adam Phillips's sense: his wandering bits work like the free play of the signifier and free association, so the stage becomes staged therapy in Lacan's return-to-Freud mode. The chapter reads the trumpet purchase as anxiety speaking through parapraxis, the street-sign and 'suck a bag of dicks' bits through Saussure's arbitrary sign and Derrida's catachresis, and Louie following Tarese home as desire that self-consciousness cannot account for.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 12. The Law of Red Rising
samples.relation: Christopher Ketcham frames the Society through jurisprudence's debate between natural and positive law, opening with Gramsci's hegemony: Reds have internalized the Golds' message that their slave toil is heroic terraforming service, becoming 'enabled martyrs' who hate rival clans rather than their rulers. He deploys Hobbes's state of nature versus state of laws (Reds live in a state of war against Mars while Golds legislate in a state of law), Locke's suggestion that a sovereign can leave some people in the state of nature, Aquinas-style higher law, and H.L.A. Hart's positivism with Bentham and Austin—a law need not be moral to be law—to argue the Golds' caste statutes are valid yet ungrounded. His coda casts Darrow as Homer Plessy: Goldness, like whiteness in Plessy v. Ferguson, is inheritable property Reds cannot claim, and because Reds who speak are hanged, the law excludes the very voices Hart himself said keep laws from becoming terrible.

samples.book: 133 - Perry Mason and Philosophy - The Case of the Awesome Attorney
samples.title: 3. Perry Mason v. Saul Goodman
samples.relation: Scalambrino compares Mason and Better Call Saul's Saul Goodman, who pull the same shady moves (Perry's evidence switching in 'The Case of the Crimson Kiss' and 'The Case of the Restless Redhead', Saul's fabricated 'pie sitting' videos) yet receive opposite moral verdicts. He frames this through natural law (Aquinas, Kant) versus legal positivism (Hobbes's command theory, Nietzsche's law as power), the audience's 'God's-eye' perspective, and the means/ends distinction, concluding provocatively that Perry's tampering is actually easier to justify from the positivist side, since he gambles on hunches without knowing his client is innocent, while the show's premises (he is already rich and famous, his clients always innocent) make the material conditions of Saul's lawyering moot for him.

samples.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
samples.title: 15. You Can’t Use My Name
samples.relation: Recounts how Hendrix changed law twice: ExperienceHendrix v. PPX (the 'You can't use my name' tapes) imported the Wrotham Park/Blake standard so breach-of-contract damages can reflect the infringer's gains rather than the victim's losses, and Experience Hendrix v. Hendrixlicensing.com used Washington's Personality Rights Act to extend postmortem publicity rights beyond the state of domicile, raising the constitutional problems Rossi identifies. The chapter then reads the dispute over whether the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' is art or noise through legal realism versus natural law theory and legal positivism — law as what courts actually enforce — and through the Institutional Theory of Art, with a Wittgensteinian cluster definition marking the essentialist route that failed.

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Uses Hans Kelsen's legal positivism — law as amoral coercive order sustained by sanction, validated by authority rather than morality — to interpret season two's competing normative systems, from Vinci's city hall to the cartel's execution of the informant Irina. Against this background it separates revenge from Hegelian retributivism, reading Velcoro's shift from killing his wife's rapist to persuading Lenny Osterman to seek exposure instead, and Frank's communicative, confessing execution of the traitor Blake, as conflicted exercises of justice. The finale's bloodshed is read through Hegel's theory of tragedy as a collision of spheres of justice, each justified in its own eyes, whose transgression may precipitate change in Vinci.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
samples.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 15. The C-Word
samples.relation: Works through the ethics of cloning and genetic selection, starting with the objection that such technologies are "unnatural": that reasoning commits the naturalistic fallacy, since following Hume you can't get an ought from an is, and human ingenuity (roads, eyeglasses, IVF) is itself part of nature. Using Nietzsche's Genealogy account of master morality — good as the noble traits of intelligence, beauty, and strength — the chapter asks whether parents would then be obliged to engineer better children, while warning where trait-selection slides: Nazi eugenics, racist trait-lists (both Leda and Castor are white and conventionally attractive), and "abilism" against the deaf. It concludes that cloning itself is not evil: Projects Leda and Castor are immoral not because they clone but because they treat clones as mere means to an end, in Kant's sense, and trample their autonomy.

samples.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
samples.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Kirkwood argues that caffeine is uncontroversially a performance-enhancing drug—boosting memory, reaction time, endurance—and that by WADA's own three-part test (performance-enhancing, potentially harmful, against the spirit of sport) coffee should count as doping, yet never has. He dismantles the standard anti-doping arguments as applied to coffee: the cheating/unfairness charge is circular and dissolves when everyone may use it; the 'unnaturalness' argument commits a non sequitur (umbrellas are unnatural too, and chewed coffee beans seem natural); and the harm test fails because the positive threshold sits at a mere 20-ounce serving, far below caffeinism. His conclusion is that coffee escapes the 'doping' label not through moral reasoning but through public acceptance—the emotive word 'drug' is withheld from the substance everyone uses.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: A Darker Shade Realism in Neo-Noir
samples.relation: Jason Holt argues that realism, especially about the role values play in people's lives, is the underappreciated essence of noir, offering a working definition of noir as 'stylized crime realism.' Surveying neo-noir detectives (Harper, Chinatown's Gittes), revamped femmes fatales who get away with it (Body Heat's Matty, The Last Seduction's Bridget), morally ambiguous protagonists (To Live and Die in L.A., Manhunter), and Lynch and Tarantino, he shows how the post-Production-Code freedom lets endings ring true to life by letting the guilty escape justice. He coins the 'normativistic fallacy' as the inverse of Moore's naturalistic fallacy: inferring what is from what ought to be, arguing that mainstream cinema's poetic justice commits it while neo-noir's downbeat endings correct it, fulfilling the realism latent in classic noir.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: Bringing Balance to the Force
samples.relation: Harter argues that Revenge of the Sith manipulates audiences into fearing the medical technology that saves Anakin on Mustafar, portraying his prosthetic transformation into Vader as horrifying when in real bioethical terms saving a burn victim with ventilators, feeding tubes, and prosthetics is something we applaud. He diagnoses Lucas's framing as the naturalistic fallacy (what is natural is good), grounded in Hume's is-ought gap, and flags the mirror-image 'technological fallacy' of assuming enhancement like General Grievous's cyborg body must be good. The chapter concludes that technology is value-neutral and its worth depends on the context of use — which is what it means for Anakin and Luke, both maimed and prosthetized, to 'bring balance to the Force.'

samples.book: 081 - How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy - Being and Awesomeness
samples.title: How I Met Your Mother and Philosophy
samples.relation: Framed as a sports broadcast with Aristotle as commentator, the chapter tests an evolutionary ethics ('BEES': the good is the naturally desirable, so the Pleistocene Stinson strategy of spreading genes grounds Barney's womanizing) against its classic critics. Hume's is-ought gap and Moore's open question argument are deployed against deriving Barney's right to pursue tail from human nature, while William Casebeer's evolutionary ethics replies that 'good' can be defined by present reproductive success - under which lying and eternal bachelorhood fail, since commitment is what reproduces genomes in urban New York ('BIRDS'). The chapter concludes that evolutionary ethics can support the Bro Code only by contestable redefinition, and the lying objection stands.

samples.book: 255 - The Godfather and Philosophy - An Argument You Can't Refute
samples.title: 1. How to De-Nazify Nietzsche’s Philosophical Anthropology
samples.relation: Golomb argues the Nazi reading of the will to power as military conquest confuses Nietzsche's Macht (sublimated spiritual power) with Kraft (brute force) and Gewalt (violence), showing through Human, All Too Human and Daybreak that self-overcoming and creative sublimation, not domination, define the Übermensch. He builds a typology of 'positive' versus 'negative' power in which the anti-Semite figures as the vengeful, ressentiment-driven 'slave,' and insists Nietzsche's morality is not naturalistic—power must be transfigured by self-education—so his anthropology stands beyond the eugenic and racial distinctions central to Nazi ideology, even in the misused 'blond beast' passage.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Sets up Sons of Anarchy as a Hamlet retelling — Jax the prince, Clay the Claudius who murdered John Teller and married Gemma, Tara a gutsier Ophelia — and reads it through Freud and Ernest Jones's Hamlet and Oedipus: Jax's protest that he 'untwisted my mommy thing a long time ago,' his toleration of Gemma's meddling, and the Season 4/5 finale tableaux where Gemma displaces Tara at his side betray an unresolved Oedipus complex. Freud's three agencies get bodies: Clay as pure Id (beating Gemma in 'Hands'), Tara as Superego, Jax as the mediating Ego, with SAMCRO itself a collective Id worshipped in its 'chapel.' Oral and anal-stage fixations explain the Sons' chain-smoking, recklessness, and defiance of authority, while the Id's civil war between libido and the death drive plays out in Gemma's post-beating sex binge and Jax's unconscious pleasure in killing.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter reads Harlan's family bonds through Freud's Oedipus Complex - Raylan bails Arlo out only at stepmother Helen's request, and Coover whimpers 'I'm sorry, Mamma' while cradled in Mags's arms after she hammers his hand, the submissive son destroyed by his need for his mother's approval. It then applies Schopenhauer's pessimism to Winona's pregnancy: if life is suffering, as On the Vanity of Existence argues, bringing a child into Harlan is selfish vanity, and Mags's dynasty-building - grooming Loretta, bequeathing the weed business - is the will-to-live seeking immortality through the family name. Only Boyd and Ava's unsentimental care for the demented Arlo, the chapter suggests, escapes both the Oedipal trap and the vanity of lineage.

samples.book: 139 - Arrested Development and Philosophy - They've Made a Huge Mistake
samples.title: Arrested Development and Philosophy
samples.relation: Runs the Bluths through Freudian psychoanalysis: George Sr. hiding in the attic ('Sad Sack', 'Good Grief!') illustrates the unconscious, preconscious, and repression; Michael acts as ego mediating the family's id demands (the unfrozen stock spree) against George Michael's super-ego; Tobias dressing as a pirate among homosexuals and Michael's 'brother...bother' and 'Egg' slips are parapraxes betraying repressed desire; Buster's Motherboy dates and 'Why I Want to Marry My Mother' enact a failed Oedipus complex; and the brothers' scheme against George Sr. in 'Making a Stand' reenacts the primal horde of Totem and Taboo, origin of the incest taboo that haunts George Michael and Maeby.

samples.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
samples.title: “Strange Magic,” Electric Light Orchestra, 1975
samples.relation: Kowalski reads the film's astral-form scenes as a dramatization of Cartesian substance dualism against Strange's opening physicalism ('There is no such thing as spirit! We are made of matter and nothing more'): the Ancient One pushing his astral body out refutes physicalism, his soul reads books while his body sleeps, and he fights Kaecilius's acolyte as a visible astral form in Christine Palmer's ER. The chapter then confronts the classic interaction problem — Descartes' pineal gland and 'animal spirits,' Elisabeth of Bohemia's and Garrett Thomson's objections — asking how an immaterial astral form can turn pages or knock over vending machines, joking that it would take 'a very strange form of interactionism.' The Ancient One's account of magic as energy drawn from other dimensions of the multiverse is offered as the film's own dualist reply, with a closing plea for the epistemic humility Strange had to learn.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Hess asks whether the monster has a soul and makes him the test case between physicalism (Kim, Churchland, van Inwagen) and dualism: recasting Frank Jackson's Mary as a color-blind monster who learns every physical fact about color vision, receives new eyes on Walton's ship, and then learns the 'what it is like' of seeing red for the first time, he argues there are nonphysical mental facts, so physicalism is false. He then runs Plantinga's argument that we are not our bodies or brains through a machine that replaces the monster's parts and hemispheres one by one while he stays conscious, and adds near-death out-of-body evidence like Maria's window-ledge shoe to suggest we can exist disembodied. The upshot is symmetric: whatever we conclude about the monster's soul we must conclude about our own - so be careful about assuming who does and does not have a soul, even monsters.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Edward Cox asks whether physicalism - everything is physical, and everything depends on the arrangement of physical stuff - is true in Westeros. The causal argument shows Jaime's love could move Bran's body only if it is itself a brain state, and the maesters' science (boiling wine against infection, Baratheon black hair as heredity, the Eyrie's winch) reveals a world running on our physics. But magic strains the picture: reanimated Othor and Jafer Flowers must physically change to walk, and Daenerys's walk into Drogo's pyre requires her resolve to disrupt combustion itself - so Cox concludes magic is either violation of physical law or a nonphysical force, and that in our world immaterial souls would be exactly as improbable as magic.

samples.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
samples.title: Girls and Philosophy
samples.relation: Carleo and D'Ambrosio read Hannah's 'busy trying to become who I am' through the classical Chinese debate over names: her self-claimed title 'writer' preceding any conduct is the Confucian nightmare of names divorced from actuality, diagnosed by the Analects's rectification of names ('rulers should rule, fathers should father') and the sheep-stealing passage warning against over-identifying with a single role. Adam, by contrast, lives the Daoist ideal - the empty vessel of the Daodejing acting by wu wei, and Zhuangzi's butterfly dream fluidity in his role-play sex and absorbed woodworking, unattached to titles. Mencius and Xunzi frame the resolution: by Season Three Hannah finally rectifies names at GQ while Adam's non-identity turns delusional, vindicating the ideal of being an 'internal sage and external king' - Daoist in private, responsible to roles in public.

samples.book: 197 - True Blood and Philosophy - We Wanna Think Bad Things with You
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: The Terjesens pit Kant's impersonal morality — Sam's contractual distance from the thieving Mickens is exactly how he would treat strangers — against Confucius and Mencius, for whom filial duties are the nursery of virtue: we learn benevolence by serving parents and revering elders, Lafayette's care for Lettie Mae and Tara shows family forming moral character, and the Upright Gong's covering for a father's sheep-stealing grounds Jason's 'sometimes the right thing to do is the wrong thing'. Mencius's King Shun, who abdicates and carries his criminal father into exile, models how Tommy and Jason should put family first while accepting the cost, while Mozi's universal love surfaces in Godric's 'forgiveness is love', and the chapter concludes that family counts only insofar as it develops our moral nature — the line between Tommy and Sam.

samples.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Decker parallels the Republic's fall into Palpatine's Empire with the Zhou dynasty's collapse that birthed Chinese philosophy, reading three Jedi from the Dark Times comics through it. K'Kruhk, guided by the Zatoichi-like Master Zao, learns wu-wei - following the Force rather than forcing outcomes, with Laozi's Dao as the Force's Chinese analogue. Dass Jennir's struggle over what 'Jedi' means after killing a slaver becomes Confucian rectification of names and the cultivation of ren, while Kai Hudorra's loss of faith, withdrawal to a casino, and final sacrificial stand against Vader embody Mozi-style pragmatic minimalism redeemed by Jennir's virtuous example.

samples.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
samples.title: The Devil and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nicolas Michaud catalogues the demonic hierarchy - de Spina's goblins, incubi, and familiars, Dante's Malebranche, Binsfeld's seven princes of Hell - through Dungeon Keeper's Dark Mistress, World of Warcraft succubi, Se7en, Hellraiser's Pinhead, Hellboy, and Spawn. His real argument is ontological: names are power, and what we call the Devil fixes how we treat him. Recovering the Hebrew sense of 'satan' as an appointed adversary and 'Lucifer' as light-bringer (compared to Prometheus), he argues the same being could be reframed from tempter to giver of knowledge, much as naming Columbus's invasion a 'discovery' launders atrocity.

samples.book: 158 - Ender's Game and Philosophy - The Logic Gate Is Down
samples.title: Ender’s Game and Philosophy
samples.relation: Morgan Deane reads Ender's tactics as Sunzi's Art of War in action: winning all future fights by terror, exploiting Bonzo's hot anger, 'fatal terrain' when Graff stacks hopeless odds, formlessness that hides intent, and fluid toon formations that move like water — all grounded in Daoist harmony with the Way and the Confucian role-duty of the general-as-father who throws soldiers into hopeless positions to win their devotion. He also finds Legalist rewards-and-punishments in Ender's command of Dragon Army, concluding Ender qualifies as a Sunzi-style military genius whose empathy is the steep moral price of victory.

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues Rust Cohle's stated pessimism and in-principle embrace of suicide closely track Schopenhauer's view that suffering is built into the world with no providential redemption, yet the two diverge because Schopenhauer condemned suicide as an affirmation of the will-to-live rather than its denial. The chapter traces Rust's three-stage arc — jaded wannabe-suicidal pessimist who nonetheless energetically investigates the Dora Lange case, resigned drinker, and finally cautious affirmer of life after the Yellow King confrontation — and contends his detective work is really motivated by a Schopenhauerian morality of compassion and justice, not mere 'programming.' Rust's finale conversion is read as an evidence-based judgment that thoroughgoing pessimism is intellectually dishonest, since compassion and justice do score nontrivial victories.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: Ride the Pink Horse Money, Mischance, Murder, and the Monads of Film Noir
samples.relation: Silver reads Robert Montgomery's Ride the Pink Horse as a prototypically noir embodiment of Schopenhauer's The World as Will and Representation. The revenge-driven Gagin, like Hugo, is enslaved to money and will—'a man can do what he wants, but not want what he wants'—and takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world, blind to the monads and Platonic-cave shadows of fate around him. Against him stand Pancho's suffering kindness and the Indian girl Pila's selfless compassion, which Silver aligns with Schopenhauer's dictum that 'compassion is the basis of all morality' and his prizing of aesthetic transcendence. The carousel (tío vivo) and the burning of Zozobra, the god of bad luck, become symbols of will's pointless circular striving from which only sacrifice and art offer escape.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Liane Heller pairs Cohen and Schopenhauer - born and died on September 21st, the autumnal equinox - as two explorers of the world's irrational negativity who both retreat to 'a room' to create. Schopenhauer's directionless Will, his pessimism about a life of constant suffering, his notorious misogyny in 'On Women,' and his ascetic denial of the will-to-live (with his contempt for Judaism and preference for the Upanishads and Buddhist compassion) are set against Cohen's affirmation that love is 'the only engine of survival,' his five-year Zen retreat that could not hold him, and his return to the Judaism of the 'little Jew who wrote the Bible.' A closing imagined dialogue has a humbled Schopenhauer confronted with Cohen's self-compassion and ordinary joys, admitting the limits of his own field of vision.

samples.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
samples.title: From Desperation to Haven
samples.relation: Held reads The Tommyknockers, Desperation, and The Regulators through Arthur Schopenhauer's pessimism, arguing King's worlds are 'always already sunk in evil' and that the will to live swings life between pain and boredom even before the supernatural arrives. He identifies egoism as the root of King's cruelty (Hilly banishing David Brown to Altair-4, Bobbi turning her dog into a battery) and offers Schopenhauer's compassion-based virtue ethic, 'injure no one; help everyone,' as the answer, supported by MacIntyre on the degradation of happiness and set against Nietzsche's 'last man' and nihilism. Gard's rescue of David Brown ('the kid matters or nothing matters') and Johnny Marinville's self-sacrifice in Desperation exemplify the heroic, compassionate life that defies the dark.

samples.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
samples.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Gregory and Tod Bassham argue Stoicism is the seaman's philosophy of agency, teaching a clear-eyed grasp of what we can control, influence, or not control at all. Using Epictetus's play metaphor and 'you will fetter my leg but not my will,' Seneca and Marcus Aurelius on fear, they map three techniques onto sailing: cheerful resignation (Gerry Spiess righting Yankee Girl, Shackleton's James Caird crew laughing amid the Southern Ocean), self-sufficiency (splicing lines, emotional independence on a cramped boat), and negative visualization / premeditatio malorum (practicing docking under sail, imagining lost rudders). Skip Allen scuttling Wildflower and Dinelli's endurance illustrate the trichotomy of control and freedom of mind.

samples.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
samples.title: 10. How to Be Free
samples.relation: O'Connell and Sirvent argue Seneca's Stoic freedom - release from fear of death and from every attachment - illuminates the two most enslaved groups in the story. The Unsullied's training strips them of possessions, names, lust, and fear, with Grey Worm's shame at fearing death for Missandei's sake showing exactly what attachment does to this freedom, while the Faceless Men's 'valar morghulis' mantra works like Seneca's recommended contemplation of death, letting Arya drink blindly from the cup at the House of Black and White. The chapter concludes that a fearlessness built by slaves and assassins really is a kind of freedom beyond their servitude, though Seneca would recoil at the brutal methods that produce it.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 4. On Being a Dead Person Who Hasn’t Died Yet
samples.relation: Mark Ralkowski argues that Louis's 'dead people who haven't died yet' bit sounds like Marcus Aurelius, and that Dr. Bigelow's Season Four advice about back pain, the three-legged dog, and heartbreak works as the Stoic spiritual exercises Pierre Hadot described - above all the 'view from above' that re-describes things to strip them to their true value. Epictetus's dichotomy of control explains Bigelow's core advice: pain is not 'up to us' but our judgments about it are, so Louie should adjust his expectations to nature ('every second without back pain is a lucky second') instead of demanding a pain-free life. The apparently un-Stoic counsel to savor heartbreak ('misery is wasted on the miserable') is defended as genuinely Stoic: viewing his lost love from the perspective of a dead-person-who-hasn't-died-yet, Louie can accept sadness as precious and impermanent rather than being crushed by it. The chapter concedes Louis is no philosopher, but suggests his bits - contrasted with Seinfeld's 'polished' version on Talking Funny - can be read as newly discovered Meditations for comedy audiences.

samples.book: 210 - Football and Philosophy - Going Deep
samples.title: Heroes of the Coliseum
samples.relation: Reid draws an extended analogy between big-time college football players and Roman gladiators—both socially marginalized entertainers, controlled by coaches/editors and crowds, risking their bodies for others' entertainment. Through Roman Stoicism (Seneca, Epictetus, Cicero) she argues virtus does not depend on external wealth, status, or freedom but on accepting fate and excelling within one's role, so exploited athletes can still be genuine heroes of virtue. Following Marcus Aurelius's distaste for the games, she concludes those with power over players' unjust conditions are morally obliged to improve them.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lopez uses the monster - 'one man made out of many' - to stress-test personal identity: brain-swap and amnesia-torture thought experiments first drive us to identify with our memories (the memory-based psychological criterion) and then, when Victor offers to wipe memory before the pain experiments, with our bodies, yielding inconsistent answers. The monster's own testimony - waking confused, prodding fire like an infant, acquiring language by eavesdropping on Safie's lessons, and building his values from scratch out of Paradise Lost and the cottagers - shows he is a genuinely new person rather than whoever once owned his corpse-parts, since we would not say a memory-wiped torture victim ceases to exist. He concludes the monster satisfies the five listed personhood criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-awareness), with identity riding a continuing stream of consciousness running on a body that is, in the end, secondary 'hardware.'

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: APPENDIX - Who are Locke, Hume, and Rousseau The Losties’ Guide to Philosophers
samples.relation: Scott Parker's appendix profiles the philosophers behind Lost's namesake characters: John Locke for the survivor (blank-slate empiricism, belief tempered by tolerance, The Reasonableness of Christianity), David Hume for Desmond (causation as habitual inference, with the button press as the image of induction, plus bundle-theory skepticism about the self), and Jean-Jacques Rousseau for Danielle ('man is naturally good, and only by institutions is he made bad,' private property as the root of inequality). It adds Jeremy Bentham (the alias on Locke's coffin), Kierkegaard via the Fear and Trembling Hurley finds under the Temple (Abraham's teleological suspension of the ethical and the leap of faith), Dogen on zazen, Edward Said for Sayid (Orientalism and the audience's own projected savagery onto the Others), and short lives of Kate Cooper Austin, Carlyle, Rutherford, Hugo Grotius, Bakunin, Ram Dass, Edmund Burke, Hawking, Minkowski, Faraday, C. S. Lewis, and Lennon.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Pötzsch reads Sheldon as the early Wittgenstein trapped in the Tractatus's picture theory — taking Penny's 'How've you been?' as a question about existence and replying 'I can't be impossible, I exist' — living among speakers of the later Wittgenstein's language games, where meaning is use within forms of life and social conventions (the tea that must be an invitation, the pizza-for-helping-moving protocol). Family resemblance, the childlike learner whose slate of social convention is blank (the Lockean tabula rasa applied to Sheldon's social mind), and lying as a language game Sheldon plays badly — the fake cousin Leopold Houston's fabricated Facebook trail, the orangutan hair — all dramatize the passage from logic-bound to use-based meaning that Sheldon, like Wittgenstein, may eventually make.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 10. Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood as Philosophy Children as Philosophers
samples.relation: Baggett argues that Mister Rogers' Neighborhood was a profoundly philosophical show because it treated very young children as natural philosophers — curious, wonder-filled questioners — rather than mere proto-adults. He frames child-development theory through the rationalism/empiricism divide (Skinner's behaviorism descending from Locke's tabula rasa, Chomsky's innatism from Descartes) and champions Gareth Matthews's claim that children's 'romancing' is genuine philosophy adults should not condescend to. Rogers modeled Hadot's philosophy-as-a-way-of-life and James's and Rousseau's active learning; episodes on death (the goldfish), work, and make-believe invited the same wonder Aquinas and Hume brought to happiness and causation, treating children as members of Kant's kingdom of ends.

samples.book: 259 - Lost and Philosophy - The Island Has Its Reasons
samples.title: NOTE
samples.relation: Shai Biderman and William J. Devlin trace John Locke the character's shift from the empiricism of his philosophical namesake to Taoism. Early Locke is the tabula-rasa empiricist and scientific-method hunter and hatch-engineer, but his miraculous restored ability to walk, Jacob's touch, and his visions push him to ask 'why' rather than 'how.' They argue Locke comes to follow the Tao—the unnamable Way symbolized by the black-and-white yin-yang seen in backgammon pieces and Claire's dream—advising Charlie via the struggling moth, teaching Walt to visualize the knife's path, and finding Sun's ring by not looking, ultimately reading his sacrificial death as effortless surrender to the island's flow.

samples.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
samples.title: 6. The Foundations of Psychohistory
samples.relation: Irish roots psychohistory in the seventeenth- and eighteenth-century clash between rationalism and empiricism over whether history can be a science. Descartes's mathematical, a priori method (which bred an 'anti-historical skepticism') is the ancestor of Seldon's dream of mathematizing human behavior, while Locke's empiricism and probabilistic knowledge inspired Gibbon's defense of historical evidence. Irish stages the Ancients-versus-Moderns debate through the Lord Dorwin / Salvor Hardin exchange over first-hand versus armchair scholarship, and contrasts Gibbon's moral, backward-looking history with Seldon's amoral, forward-looking prediction.

samples.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
samples.title: 17. Our Lying Eyes
samples.relation: Wood asks how Elliot - and we, who see only what he sees - can know anything, and contrasts two empiricisms: Locke's white-paper mind furnished by ideas copied from mind-independent objects, which explains Mr. Robot as perceptual error, and Berkeley's idealism, on which only ideas and their divine cause exist, which makes Elliot's unshared hallucination of Mr. Robot dangerously hard to distinguish from reality. Consistency of perception is the only test left, and it fails Elliot until the pier video proves no one pushed him - and fails us again when his cozy Season Two routine turns out to be prison.

samples.book: 271 - Fatherhood – Philosophy for Everyone - The Dao of Daddy
samples.title: FATHERHOOD PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
samples.relation: Florell and Wilson, psychologists, survey parenting through the nature–nurture debate, casting Locke's tabula rasa against Rousseau's noble-savage view of children, alongside Piaget and Kohlberg on moral development and Walter Mischel's marshmallow experiment on impulse control. They map the four parenting styles (authoritarian, permissive, uninvolved, authoritative) on responsiveness and control, argue authoritative parenting is optimal, and advise fathers to adjust discipline to each child's innate temperament rather than enforce rigid gender roles.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 1. Finding the Meaning of Life in Downton Abbey
samples.relation: Blessing pits Steve Jobs's 'Do What You Love' creed (and Oprah's 'follow your bliss') against Downton's world of inherited roles, where nobody from Anna to Lady Mary chooses their work. She distinguishes happiness from meaningfulness, since Matthew's war wounds and Mary's grief over his death are painful yet deeply meaningful, and tests subjectivist theories such as Nietzsche's meaning-as-passionate-process against Nozick's demand that a meaningful life leave permanent traces and Susan Wolf's hybrid 'loving objects that are worthy of love.' Kant's duty to develop one's talents rather than idle for pleasure, and Lord Grantham's self-description as 'a custodian, not an owner,' anchor the show's counter-ethos of duty over desire, embodied in Carson, Mrs. Hughes, and Mrs. Patmore's pride in unloved, socially necessary work. The chapter concludes that Downton validates hard honest work as an end in itself, challenging the narcissism of the 'holy You' and expressive individualism.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 1. Finding the Meaning of Life in Downton Abbey
samples.relation: Blessing tests the Steve Jobs/Oprah 'do what you love' creed against Downton, where rigid class structure assigns nearly everyone a role they did not choose. She distinguishes happiness from meaningfulness (Matthew's war wounds, Mary's grief after his death) and purposefulness (Grantham's custodian speech), then weighs subjectivist theories of meaning, including Nietzsche's idea that meaning arises from the passionate process itself, against Nozick's permanence view and Susan Wolf's hybrid 'subjective attraction meets objective attractiveness,' adding Kant's duty to develop one's talents against a world of idle pleasure. She concludes that the Abbey's ethos - Grantham as custodian not owner, Carson's pride in service, Patmore's kitchen, 'I have no right to be unhappy' - shows that socially necessary work one does not love can still make a meaningful life, while DWYL is elitist and narcissistic.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 8. Living for More
samples.relation: Kevin McCain separates meaning of life—why humans exist at all, with no creator-God found in Gold nihilism ('the Golds have no God'), the Obsidians' manufactured Norse religion, or the Reds' Vale and Old Man—from meaning in life, following Susan Wolf's distinction. After rejecting supernaturalism and pessimistic naturalism (Nero's universe that 'does not notice us,' met by Karnus's Camus-like defiant pride and Thomas Nagel's ironic stance), he rejects Richard Taylor's subjectivism via the Sisyphus story: Karnus and the Boneriders enjoy their cruelty, but enjoying it does not make their lives meaningful. Wolf's objectivism wins—a meaningful life is actively and lovingly engaged in projects of worth—which is exactly Darrow's living for more, contrasted with the Jackal's loveless, self-loathing pursuit of mattering.

samples.book: 092 - Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy - Last Exit from Litchfield
samples.title: Orange Is the New Black and Philosophy
samples.relation: Duffy applies Susan Wolf's formula (subjective attraction meeting objective attractiveness) to Red's cooking, Poussey's friendship, and Taystee's library work, arguing these women meet the conditions yet still cannot live meaningful lives because Litchfield hands out 'chickens': WAC, the mock job fair, and the yard chicken are illusions of meaning designed to keep inmates quiet, as Healy admits with his bath-before-dinner analogy. Only projects that change the prison's conditions themselves, Piper's newsletter sting and Soso's hunger strike, are genuinely meaningful, and the yogic dharma of non-attachment (Yoga Jones's mandala advice) is a survival tool, not a substitute. She closes that guards too can find meaning, and have an obligation, in rehabilitating rather than punishing.

samples.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
samples.title: 7. Eleanor and the Meaning of Afterlife
samples.relation: Builds a dilemma from 'Existential Crisis': Michael's prospective retirement (via Todd May's Death) makes finitude look meaning-destroying, while the humans' endless existence — 802 reboots, Mindy St. Claire's eternal Cannonball Run II in the Medium Place — threatens boredom and disconnection from past selves. Testing God-free answers, it runs through Camus's Sisyphus, Richard Taylor's desire-fulfillment view, Susan Wolf's requirement that we love what deserves to be loved (Eleanor's philosophy study, friendship with Tahani, romance with Chidi), and John Martin Fischer on free authorship and narrative order (Eleanor's note to herself in What We Owe to Each Other). Conclusion: Eleanor and friends can lead meaningful lives even if damned and repeatedly rebooted.

samples.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
samples.title: Girls and Philosophy
samples.relation: Blessing and Wezowiczi test theories of life's meaning on the two narcissists of Girls: Hannah, whose purpose-driven pursuit of being a writer (manufacturing experiences, ignoring her father's medical procedure) shows that goal achievement alone collapses into Taylor's and Camus's Sisyphus problem, and Jessa, whose 'life addict' desire-satisfaction illustrates the Nietzschean live-in-the-moment view the authors find reckless and irresponsible. Using Wielenberg's excrement-eater and the subjectivist/objectivist debate, they land on Susan Wolf's 'loving objects that are worthy of love,' then argue via Socrates's examined life and Sartre's bad faith that neither Hannah's phony narrative nor Jessa's protective persona counts as authentic, examined living.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 60. Little Women as Philosophy Death or Marriage and the Meaning of Life
samples.relation: The chapter tests Susan Wolf's 'fitting fulfillment' theory (meaning as subjective attraction meeting objective attractiveness) against Greta Gerwig's Little Women, arguing the March sisters and most historical women are ill-fitted to it. Jo is forced to make her writing 'mercenary and commercial' and marries; Amy abandons painting and marries Laurie because 'marriage is an economic proposition'; Marmee, Hannah, and Mrs. Hummel live from duty and self-sacrifice without joy. Invoking Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but becomes a woman' and Imposter Syndrome, it concludes fulfillment is indicative but not necessary for meaning, urging a purely objective theory that can value women's lives 'appropriately appreciated at least in principle.'

samples.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
samples.title: 7. Eleanor and the Meaning of Afterlife
samples.relation: Yang frames Eleanor's predicament as a dilemma: a finite life seems drained of value by its ending, while an immortal one collapses into boredom or into the disconnection of the 802 memory-wiped reboots. Camus's Sisyphus and Richard Taylor's desire-fulfillment view prove inadequate, so he adopts Susan Wolf's account of meaning as loving what deserves to be loved, which Eleanor's study of moral philosophy, her friendships, and her romance with Chidi satisfy even without God or eternity. John Martin Fischer's narrative approach then redeems the reboots as self-contained episodes, and Eleanor's note to herself in Scanlon's book shows memory wipes need not sever the story of a life.
